newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. army base workers strike in Germany.
newsitem.headline: U.S. army base workers strike in Germany.

text.p: Thousands of civilian workers at U.S. army bases went on strike on Tuesday to press demands for better work conditions as U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen arrived in Germany.

Nearly 4,000 members of Germany's OeTV public services union and DAG white-collar workers union went on strike for the second straight day in several towns and cities and brought numerous workplaces to a standstill, OeTV union leader Walter Keppler said.

"It is no coincidence that we are on strike as U.S. Defence Secretary Cohen visits Germany," Keppler told Reuters. "It is in our interests to make him aware of the situation of civilian workers at U.S. military bases here."
There are about 35,000 mostly German civilian employees working as support staff for the 75,000 U.S. troops in Germany.

Workers in Heidelberg, Mannheim, Schweinfurt, Ansbach, Augsburg in the south, as well as in western and central Germany took to the streets in protest at work conditions which they say are inferior to those in German firms.

The U.S. army was not immediately available for comment but the U.S. forces' Stars and Stripes newspaper reported that U.S. officials were playing down the impact the strike was having on military communities.
It said that in places like motor pools and public works -- where local employees made up most of the work force -- business could be severely slowed or even halted.

Keppler said unions had been trying to hammer out a new wage agreement to increase job security and benefits for redundancies and that the U.S. military authorities had failed to come up with satisfactory offers.
"We want to keep up pressure to persuade the U.S. forces to come to the negotiating table and come up with a decent offer," Keppler said.
Unions are also angry that the cash-strapped forces plan to increasingly hire out projects to contractors.
Cohen, on his first visit to Europe since taking office, was due to meet German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe and Chancellor Helmut Kohl and to visit American troops at the Hohenfels training base.

He will also meet U.S. Army General George Joulwan, supreme allied commander of all NATO forces in Europe (SACEUR), and be briefed by other top American military officers at the U.S. Army's European Command Headquarters in Stuttgart.
